utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Could you kindly inform the witness that he may have to wait a little bit until we process preliminary issues that I was told we are to expect. So, Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, ma'am. The accused are all here. Defence teams seem to be okay, except for Mr. Sarapa is still not here. And for the Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey, and Ms. Soljan. I understand you have some preliminaries, both of you. Is that correct? Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honour, that's correct. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for having to bring this motion or oral request at this time, but it has been brought to our attention late last night that -- and unfortunately it's a repeated problem that we brought to the attention of the Court, and that's what we believe, and most respectfully to the Prosecution, their continued violation of this Court's order and 65 ter. In this instance, however, it's not the same motion because we believe it's somewhat a grosser violation because the Prosecutor in their disclosures to the Court and through the EDS system lists eight documents that they are going to use with three exhibits they're going to use with the present witness, Mr. Egbers. Yesterday at the conclusion of Mr. Egbers's testimony I confirmed with the Madam Prosecutor who is leading the witness. She confirmed that she's not going to play a video tomorrow which is not on her list of disclosed documents. That was approximately 1.45 or so. Yesterday afternoon at about 3.15, upon leaving for our visitation with our client, we received a phone call that a video was going to be played. Then late last night at approximately 7.45 we visited with the Office of the Prosecutor, specifically both Mr. McCloskey and Madam Soljan, if I'm saying it correctly. I apologise to her --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't even pronounce your own name correctly, so I'm not surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't even pronounce your own name correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought my English was actually fairly good, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But to say that Ostojic is Ostojic --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've been saying it that way for 45 years. So if you'd like me to say Ostojic I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But all kidding aside, Your Honour, it's a very serious request on our behalf. It's a repeated violation. I know my fellow colleagues from the Defence have raised it on numerous occasions. We have two pending motions before the Court that we're waiting to get resolved on this issue. We think this actually is a blatant and direct violation. Not only do they fail to place it on the list of documents that they're going to use with this witness, but after confirming -- just to repeat, yesterday at the end of the day they confirmed they will not be using video transcripts and it specifically relates to the identification, or purported identification, of our client, Mr. Beara. We looked at that video. We have other arguments on that I'd like to reserve them for our reply anticipating what they may say in the response. Again, I must stress that it's not because of an identification of our client. This witness has identified him; we think poorly. We disagree that he met Mr. Beara. We don't have to go into those arguments. Hopefully we'll draw that through the cross-examination. However, we think that the tactic used is what's the violation, and we need to at least get some guidance from the Court as to how we're going to proceed, and I think this may be an opportune time to set those guidelines and restrict or prohibit the Prosecution from violating these guidelines what I believe anyway is almost with every witness thus far. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you sit down, Mr. Ostojic, I'd like you to articulate precisely which documents are you referring to, because you mentioned initially eight documents and then you specifically pointed out the video, and it's not yet clear in my mind whether the Prosecution intends to make use of this video or not because initially they said they would, then they said they wouldn't. What's the position as you obtained it at 7.45 p.m. yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That they will use the video that is not on their disclosure documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And the other documents, are there any other documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There is no other problem. These eight, they've produced them timely, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Soljan or Mr. McCloskey. I don't know. I see you arguing amongst yourself who would --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I will go ahead, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I believe this is more an issue of misunderstanding, although I do fully accept the responsibility for not putting on the video on the exhibit list. I only noticed that in the course of the day yesterday. And then we indicated that as soon as we were aware of this to the Defence for Mr. Beara, and indeed then in the evening at 7.45 showed them a few times the excerpts of this video. Now, for the record I can just indicate that this video is 65 ter number 2025, and it is a video that is referred to in the April 30th, 2000, interview that Lieutenant Colonel Egbers had with the ICTY, the ERN for that being 00946484. It's ERN V00-1957. That that video is in fact mentioned within the statement, and there's a short description that Mr. Egbers gives of Mr. Beara, identifying Mr. Beara in this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you will agree that the statement itself is not part record or is not an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The statement itself is not an exhibit, but it has been offered, and the Defence has been on notice about all the statements, ICTY statements of Mr. Egbers. The video itself has a 65 ter number. It was disclosed on the 19th of December, 2005, and it was then -- and then the 65 ter list itself was disclosed in April 2006 of this year. So the Defence has been on notice about this. I do apologise about the fact that this was not on the actual Prosecution exhibit list that we gave to the Defence before Mr. Egbers went on. However, as Defence for Mr. Beara itself, as Mr. Ostojic himself said, we don't believe it's at dispute that Mr. Beara was identified by Colonel Egbers, and we will not go into the -- into the details of that right now. However, we thought it would be helpful for the Court to see in fact what this tape was that identified him. That is my submission at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try and be brief and to the point, Your Honour. If you look at their 65 disclosures under 2025, under the section of description it states: "Krstic and Kovacevic in Potocari, Jovovic at Motorola, or on Motorola." It doesn't mention Mr. Beara at all. Second and most important point, the identification with this video. We've looked at that video, and we've tried to analyse that video. If nothing, without arguing but I'll have to, it's suggestive. It was an improper photo line-up by the Prosecution. This witness attempts at least seven or eight times and only after the seventh and eighth time purportedly confirms that that's Mr. Beara. Last night we were given a new and enhanced and original video that this witness didn't even look at apparently yet which has a clearer picture. What's prejudicing us is that if this witness's credibility, as all witnesses' credibilities are at issue, which video did he really examine? The video that my learned colleague is referring to under the 65 ter number it's impossible, in my view, to denote who the character is that the witness claims to be Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't you think that all this could be covered on cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't you think that all this could be covered by you on cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes and no. Here's why, Your Honour: Yes, if they use the exact same video that I have in my possession that they claim that the witness used; but no, if they slip a different video in or a completely different document. But even more importantly than our suggesting -- and respectfully to Your Honours suggesting that we have the alternative to allow the Prosecution to daily violate the rules and to submit documents and evidence in, and all the Defence has to do is cross-examine. I believe it's a strict violation of your rules, of these rules in the Tribunal. If it doesn't mean anything to have 65 ter or to produce documents in advance of trial so the Defence can be prepared, then that may be the standard and we'll accept it, but we haven't heard that ruling yet. The photo ID is also, as I said earlier, suggestive. It was improper, inappropriate. Cross-examination really shouldn't be the place to answer those questions. It should be done in advance. We would do it in advance had we had any timely notice that they were going to use this video with this witness, which they did not give us until 7.45 last night. And finally I want to say there is no misunderstanding. My learned friend says there's a misunderstanding. That's not accurate. I came up to her after the discussion yesterday, after the testimony of Mr. Egbers, and I asked her point-blank, "Are you going to use anything else or any videos?" And she answered, "I will not use any videos tomorrow." Two and a half hours later or so, we were contacted with the change of mind for whatever reason. It's not misunderstanding on my part. That's a completely different and a change in their strategy. So I take exception to categorising it as a misunderstanding. I didn't misunderstand anything. I heard her loud and clear. And they changed their mind late, only to prejudice Mr. Beara and the Defence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll come back to you on this very soon. Any further preliminary matters you wish to raise? Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] -- that the video concerns our client, but we haven't even got notice or information about this video, that this video would be used actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you speaking for yourself or the rest of the Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm speaking on behalf of General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what about the other Defence teams? Were you put on notice? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Morning, Mr. President. Want to -- I'm very often on my feet, so I wanted to refrain from doing so this morning, but indeed we support the motion presented by my colleague Mr. Ostojic, or Ostojic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We support Madam Fauveau, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And so do we. And so do we, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were not put on notice? Is that what you're saying, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We haven't been informed. It doesn't concern our client at all, but we were not -- as matter of truth, we were not informed about this video. It wasn't on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Again, we'll come back on this. Any further preliminary matters unrelated to this?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll just to indicate, Your Honour, we obviously didn't hear anything of this either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I might as well make it a full house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Thank you, Mr. Haynes. So that's it. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. One other small matter. But, Your Honour, I would -- on the video just as Ms. Soljan said, this video was given to the Defence a long time again. This has been an historic video in the previous cases of Mladic, of Krstic. It's a big ceremony. I wish we had identified it better in the index, but they need to look at the videos we give them. It's been right there for a long time. And yes, it was inadvertent; we did not put it on the list. But I think this is our first time that we haven't put something on the list after all these witnesses, so we will make mistakes and this is one of those. And before I get into the other matter, perhaps we should hear from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Finish what --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just on a scheduling matter, we -- we have another witness after this, Mr. Groenewegen. He will be a 92 ter witness and be pretty short, and so there's a chance, and we may finish with him tomorrow before we're through. We were trying to find another officer that's in the next schedule, Koster, but he -- the one day he's not available is Friday. So we may finish right on time, but we may finish a little early as well without another witness. I wanted to tell you that right now. We've been finishing a little earlier than we had expected, and we haven't been able to catch up with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- one thing I need to be clarified from you. I take it that of course you've been repeating it, both Ms. Soljan and yourself, that this P2025 was disclosed way back in December of 2005. It seems to me that part of Mr. Ostojic's complaint today, his complaint is twofold. One is the non-insertion in the 65 ter list of the video. The other thing it seems to me that he's complaining about is that the witness -- the video that you wish to tender today is not the same video that was shown to the witness when he was interviewed by your office or by your investigators. So are we talking of two separate, different videos or the same one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can answer that, and that was perhaps when we said "misunderstanding," there may have been a little misunderstanding on that. I tried to make clear to Mr. Ostojic last night the -- we have -- this was shown several years ago, before computerised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one, the first one which was used --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The original video that was shown to the witness - excuse me, Your Honour - was shown to this witness several years ago in a VCR with a television attached, and -- as far as I can recall. I don't know if I was present or not, but that's all we had back then, really. And we have gone down to the evidence room. We've gotten the original VHS tape and that is what we intend to show you, the actual tape that the witness saw. Now, we showed that to -- to the Defence team last night on the old equipment, the kind of equipment that the witness would have seen it on, so they got a good chance to see the quality of it, or lack thereof. In addition to that, we several months ago obtained a better quality copy of that -- of that video which we have given the Defence as well. However, it's a CD and you have to play it through a computer, and when this video comes out on a computer screen, it's -- it's greatly degraded from if you see it on a TV screen. We're getting a DVD for them right now so that they can see the best quality video, but that really is aside from the issue of the original video and the original ID. Just to put this in total context, the witness has always said he met a person by the name of Beara, and then he was shown this videotape and says, "Yes, that is the man I met," based on certain physical attributes. Ms. Soljan has always intended to ask this witness, "Did you see a video, and did you identify somebody from it?" And he will always say, "Yes." What was inadvertently missed was that it's best for the Court to be able to see this video so that you can compare his -- his ID to what you see on the video. And once that was realised and focused on, we went to the Defence and said, "We're sorry for the mixed messages. We need to play this individual." And they understood that and we might have some other misunderstandings, but I think that's the issue before you today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The P2025 that was disclosed to the -- part of the Defence is the -- not the one that -- the one which has been now found which is of much better quality, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. It would have been more toward -- it would have been much closer to the original, but it was probably done on a CD format that if they play in a computer it will be -- it's degraded. In fact, I think we'd all agree the one that we gave to them is not as good a quality as when you put in the original video and play it on a TV. That's why it was important for us to do that, so they understood that. But that's just the nature of discovery and electronic issues and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Judge Prost would like to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify, because I'm still not clear here. There is no dispute, I take it, that the exhibit was on the 65 ter list, but what is in dispute is the description, as you indicated, Mr. Ostojic, and the actual list for exhibits with this witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Judge. And I think we'll agree on that. If you're asking him directly, I'm sorry, you were looking at me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: No. I was looking -- first from the Prosecution and then perhaps Mr. Ostojic if you could -- you're confirming that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. This video is a segment of different videos that got that rough description and it did not include Beara. And that's unfortunate, because it would have better drawn their attention to it. But it is on the 65 ter, and I think we'll probably agree on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do in part agree but I only add two points. One, the video that we received was completely distorted, and it was not only very difficult but almost impossible to even come close to the description that the witness made in his 2000 statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. So we were convinced that it was an error. We knew that they wouldn't use that, even though this witness claims that he had met or was introduced to Mr. Beara at some time earlier. We dispute that as well. I do take exception, if I may, and I'm not sure if I answered your question, to a couple of comments that the Prosecutor Mr. McCloskey said, and he states on page 8 on line 19 and 20: "But they need to look at the videos we give them. It's been right there for a long time." It's offensive for two reasons. One, it's offensive professionally. And what they need to do is to be honest with the Court and then they need to be honest with the Defence as well. They've known for a long time that they had this refined or better imagery of this video. They never offered it to us because they're playing their trial tactics and would always like to surprise the Defence in order to push us against the wall. Their tactics -- and Mr. McCloskey's wrong to say this is the first witness we've failed to do that. It wasn't. He's made oral motions before this Court to add 65 ter documents, to present them with witnesses. My problem is this: We've believed, and we have reviewed it, that it is not Mr. Beara. And that is what they want us to argue, so that this Court can have some doubt as to whether or not it is Mr. Beara, so that this Court can say we're really curious now, and we want to see what it is. Based on Mr. Egbers description, it's impossible that he met or saw Mr. Beara. What they should do, what every Prosecutor does, either ask the Court for leave to do an in-court line-up or they should have given him a photo book with all pictures of men similarly situated. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. No, Mr. Ostojic. That's what we are here for, to hear your submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One brief question to Mr. Ostojic. You do not dispute the Prosecution's allegation that in his statement Mr. Egbers had said that he had met Mr. Beara, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I do not. That exists in the statement, that's correct. In three statements it does exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before we deliberate and decide on this, the video that was actually shown to Lieutenant Colonel Egbers when he was interviewed by the OTP, is it available in the same format as it was then? In case we need to -- to see both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge. Yes. It's in fact in the booth in a VCR. The problem is it's going to go through this system, and I just -- I saw it earlier this morning and it's degraded. But I had the television right outside as well, and we can pop that television in front of you if we can find a plug and play it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Scheduling matter we don't need to respond on that. Are there any other preliminary matters? Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- yes, Your Honour. I want just to tell you that the format that the accusation is talking about is not the format that we've had. We got this on a DVD or a CD-ROM, not on a VCR cassette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any further preliminaries? None. We have one issue that we would like to alert you to and we will be handing down a very quick oral decision now. You will -- both sides recall that in our decision of the -- dealing with the Rule 92 bis submissions, we had dealt with the transcripts of a few or several DutchBat witnesses which the Prosecution was proposing, or were proposing under Rule 92 bis, and these transcripts included reference to Nikolic. Because the Prosecution's reply did not clarify that these references were indeed to Momir Nikolic and not to the accused, we admitted the transcripts in redacted form, as you will recall, saying: "Accordingly, this evidence is only admissible under Rule 92 bis with the references to Nikolic redacted or with some formal acknowledgement by the Prosecution that the references are not to the accused in this case." In its submission, the Prosecution now confirms that -- when I say the -- in its submission, the fine -- most recent submission filed on the -- on the 12th of September, now confirms that the references to Nikolic appearing in the written evidence of four DutchBat witnesses are indeed references to Momir Nikolic and not to the accused in this case. This simplifies the admission of full transcripts pursuant to Rule 92 bis (D) which the Prosecution reports it will now be submitting. We actually have decided to accept the formal acknowledgement of the Prosecution in the submission that the -- that the Nikolic referred to is Momir Nikolic and not the Nikolic accused in this case, and that we will consequently be issuing a very brief order admitting the unredacted transcripts. Before we had redacted them slightly by deleting the name or the surname Nikolic. Now they will be in their original and -- original format. This being so, we believe unless you have reason to disagree with us, Mr. McCloskey, that this action now moots this -- the request to admit these four transcripts pursuant to Rule 92 ter or 89(F). In other words, by the -- reversing the redaction that we ordered previously, we have eliminated, as we see it, the need to have -- to decide your motion or your submission to have the same transcripts admitted under Rule 92 ter or 89(F). Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't finished, but let -- because I assume you want to address this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, it was just on this specific point. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then sit down. Thank you. Okay. This leaves three other witnesses for whom the Prosecution is still seeking admission of the transcript pursuant to Rule 92 ter and 89(F). Yes. And I think we will be dealing with that as we process the rest of the submission, but at least you know that as far as the other documents are concerned they are now being admitted in an unredacted format. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, that's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for being a bit early on my feet earlier on. But I just wanted to confirm that we are now drafting our response to the Prosecution's motion, and this is what we were suggesting indeed, to simply get the unredacted versions admitted. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Bourgon, for your cooperation. I think we need to withdraw for a few minutes to deliberate on the issue raised earlier, and I believe we will be back within a minute or two. Thank you. --- Break taken at 9.33 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let me try and summarise our decision to the best of our -- of my ability. The position as we see it is twofold. Firstly is the aspect relating to P2025 as being a document disclosed to the Defence and included in the 65 ter list of documents intended to be used in the course of this trial. From that aspect, there can be no doubt that the Prosecution can make full use of this video in the course of the trial. But the question that was raised obviously relates to the guideline that we had given in relation to our desire that prior to the arrival of each witness the parties seeking to bring forward that witness should hand over to the other party and to us a list of the exhibits that they intend to use with that particular witness. The situation as we see it is that this is the desiderate. This is what you should all try to achieve and to conform yourselves with, but it also allows for oversights that can happen from time to time, and provided such oversights are not such that would cause an undue prejudice to the other party, our position is that if it is related or an integral part of the evidence that the party seeks to tender, then should be the -- that it should be admitted, and of course every effort will be made to ensure that no prejudice is suffered. In this particular case, we see what is very relevant is the fact that there seems to be at least two versions of this same video. We want to safeguard the possibility for both of you, both Prosecution and Defence, in case the need arises, and also for ourselves, because we may come ourselves to the conclusion that we may need to see both, that both videos are made available, assuming that the witness could be asked questions relating to what he was actually shown when he was first interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution. So our decision is yes, please, Prosecution, and this will later apply also to you, try to be as diligent as you can, because when you're not the end result is three-quarters of an hour wasted, and problems and possible friction between the parties. So I enjoin you to -- to -- I'm not speaking to you, Ms. Soljan, just Prosecution in general, to make every effort to have the list, 65 ter list, related to each witness as -- as complete as possible. Of course, it is understood that at times you can have new evidence that has been dug up, but please try to communicate the complete list to the other party as early as possible. And make sure that both videos are available for whatever use either you or the Defence or ourselves may feel the need to. Right. Thank you. So let's bring the witness in. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just one error in the transcript at page 7, line 13, 14, 15, what I said is that this video does not specifically involve my client, and in the transcript it says the opposite, the opposite, that this video involves our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, Ms. Fauveau. I vividly remember you saying that it does not in fact. Thank you. And in fact, there were other counsel that repeated exactly the same. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My apologies to you for having kept you waiting for three-quarters of an hour, but we had some important procedural matters to deal with and decide upon completely unrelated to you, so you don't have to worry about what we were discussing. You're still testifying pursuant to the solemn declaration that you made yesterday, and I think on that score we can proceed. Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Egbers.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, yesterday we left off on the 12th of July and your description about what was happening at Kladanj at the demarcation point. Could you just briefly repeat for us how many buses, if you recall, were at Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I -- when I got there there were 14 buses, and only three of them were going to -- to a point where they had to get out, and then the empty buses, they drove away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you estimate how many people were coming out of those buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the first buses there were, let's say, 50 people per bus. Because it was the first convoy, it was all well organised. And there were, let's say, 50, 60 people in each bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in what direction were the people from these buses going?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw them going through a check-point, a road. I don't know where the road led to. It was said to go to Bosnia, to Muslim areas. So it was in the -- in -- for them it was a safe road, a road to safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did you have a clear impression of the state of mind of the persons coming off of those buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you yesterday, there were -- there were a lot of people frightened to be killed in the woods because we couldn't nearly see a border or something like that. The only thing we saw was a wood, and the people were very, very frightened, and they didn't know what happened -- could happen to them as they -- they were glad to see me at that time wearing a UN uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Approximately what time of day was this on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the late afternoon. Beginning of the evening. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when all buses were empty, we tried to get back to -- to the compound, back to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you say "we," are you talking just about your car?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about my car and my colleague next to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. So did you manage indeed to return?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did. Night was falling, so it was for us the way to -- to the area about Nova Kasaba, Milici, it was for us not very hard to drive through, and when we reached the environs of Nova Kasaba, it was very hard of course to go through but we reached the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. On your way through Nova Kasaba, did you pass the football field you had previously testified about?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I passed it on my left side, and I saw still men on the football field that evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So would you say that it was a scene very much similar to what you had seen earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, let me focus your attention on the next day, the 13th of July, when you were back in Potocari. The next morning did you receive an assignment again?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had to report with the captain who was in charge of escorting the convoys, and I was given the -- I guess it was number three, convoy number three, to escort all the way to Kladanj again. So I had to be ready.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then I left headquarters, and of course there were thousands of men, women, and it was very hard, as you -- as you understand. And then I saw a terrible thing at the "White House." Can I tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because upside the road there is a house, and when I saw one of the -- one of the women screaming towards the soldiers, towards us, I just went there, and I ask her what was going on. And she said, "Well, my man was taken by that house." So I -- I went to the two soldiers who were there in the neighbourhood of the house, and I said, "Well, check out the house. Let's see what's in the house."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you say "soldiers," you're referring to DutchBat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To DutchBat soldiers, yes. But there were -- those two soldiers didn't have any permission to go to -- inside the house because there were armed BSA soldiers standing in front of that house. But again because I was a lieutenant at that time, I pointed at my shoulder. I wanted them to know that I was just entering the house, whether they wanted or not. So I entered the house. I went up and I saw in every room men sitting and waiting for things to happen there. They were very, very scared, of course. That's -- when I remember it, I can still see the faces in front of me. Those men were gathered there and women and children were pushed inside the buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you have a conversation or a discussion with any of the Bosnian Serb soldiers who were at this house? About what was happening.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the men, they were very scared, and they asked us -- they asked me what -- what will happen to them, and they were -- I told them in my -- my English that I had escorted a convoy to Kladanj, and then -- they then realised that Kladanj was -- was the road to safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How were you communicating with these men?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've then spoken a few words of -- of Serbo-Croatian language and of course a bit in English and with my hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sign language.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sign language, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian Serb soldiers tell you anything about what was going on?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked them what happened to these men, why are they separated from the women, and they told me that they would be in a -- in a convoy to Kladanj as well as convoy number four. So I told the men that they would be brought by the Bosnian Serbs to Kladanj so that they could join their wives and families again. But at that time, unfortunately the men, they didn't believe me, and they said, "No." And they made the same sign the women the day before made, with the finger, you know, as you described it yesterday, along their throat. And I then told them, "Well, no, the Bosnian Serbs told me that you will be brought by Kladanj, and I had to make sure that there is an escort for you who will try to be with the buses as you go to Kladanj."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So did you indeed see these men being taken out of the "White House" and placed into buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I saw them enter three buses, I think. Together there were, let's say, 150 to 200 men inside convoy number four.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And just to clarify, you only saw the men inside the houses; is that correct? Captured men inside the houses.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I entered the house, I saw captured men inside the house and in the garden of the house there were -- there was stuff that belonged to the men, bags they've got -- they carried, and it was all in front of house. So when I entered the house I saw them. They were very scared, and I tried to -- to give them the information the Bosnian Serbs gave me, that they would be brought to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And how did these men look when they were getting onto the buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were very, very scared. When you look at their eyes, you can see that. You can tell that. And they didn't believe me, and they said, "No, we don't live another day," by -- by the signal. So they -- they were very, very scared.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And to clarify for the record, when you talk about the signal, it is the sign that you were referring to yesterday also, which was drawing the right forefinger -- or the forefinger from the left side to the right side across the neck. What did that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This thing that you described is correct and it indicated that, yes, they would be killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness could clarify the meaning of "captured men." Being detained in the "White House," being separated from their families, or they're captured as -- separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: If you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw men taken from their families. Their families went into the bus, and the men were separated and were detained inside the "White House," and there were Bosnian Serb soldiers standing in front of the "White House." So they had no -- they couldn't move. They were there detained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, do you know what happened to the convoy of these three buses that left with the men from the "White House"?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure that there was an escort, and there was a lieutenant with -- with another UN peacekeeper driving with this convoy, but unfortunately it didn't reach Kladanj. It -- it was said to me that there was an AK-47 to the head of the two soldiers who were accompanying this escort -- sorry, accompanying this convoy, and they didn't get further than Bratunac. And I don't know what happened to the men after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now what happened next? You were still in Potocari then?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I escorted the convoy number four all the way to Kladanj, and again I saw coming through Bratunac all these people on the streets celebrating, and I saw a lot more infantry standing on the road all the way to Nova Kasaba and to Milici. I was stopped several times, and because of our experience we didn't take any weapons because they would have taken our pistols and our guns, so we were there unarmed as an observer, and we were stopped, and they wanted -- they claimed our helmets and our bullet-proof vests and other stuff we had in our cars.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, were you taking the same route as the day before?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was exactly -- exactly same route. We just followed the buses again. The bus drivers knew exactly where to go to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And approximately how many buses were in the convoy that you were escorting on this day, on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same. I think about 10 to 12 to 14 buses. I didn't count them that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Convoy number three or four?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Is this particularly convoy number three that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my convoy that I escorted. And I guess -- I'm not sure about it. I have to look it up. But it's my -- there was a convoy, I thought that that was number four that had all the men inside, and my convoy had another number. It was number 3 or number four, but I have to look it up if you want to be sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned earlier on that your helmets and your bullet-proof vest was taken. Who took them?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, along the road there was a lot of infantry gathered, and they -- they stop the car. They aimed their -- their guns at us and they stop the car. They -- they are Bosnian Serb infantry units that stopped us and took the things we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you recall where along the road this took place?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the way from Bratunac to the cross-point. It's called Pusmulici. I don't remember that name, but I saw that yesterday on a map. If you want to, I could point it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. We can show you the map for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if we could just show ter -- 65 ter number 2111, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, could you try and indicate -- [French on English channel].

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are receiving interpretation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. The interpreter was on the wrong channel. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we need to go through that again for -- but it's in the transcript. The witness himself may not have been able to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you could please show to us, then, indicate by the stylus whereabouts you were stopped and your helmet and bullet-proof vests were taken from you.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you said you were seeing infantry soldiers in the area. Could you -- could you tell approximately how many soldiers there were along this road?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were hundreds of soldiers on the road all the way to Konjevic Polje and to Milici, and more. There were more soldiers than the day before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And how were they placed along the road?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had their guns on the woods in the south, and from -- so they were facing the enclave. So everybody who had to cross the road was stopped by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And were they firing on this day? Did you hear any shooting or ...

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard them firing that night but not at -- at that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did you hear any firing coming out of the woods which they were facing?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear any firing coming out of the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, on your route with -- along with the convoy, did you pass the football field in Nova Kasaba again?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I passed the football field on my right, and there were still men on the football field and men who were brought towards the football field at the day before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Were they being escorted?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were escorted by Bosnian Serbs infantry. I saw men walking by the road, on the road, with their hands on their neck towards the football field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And could you estimate the numbers of that day? How many -- how many were there at the football field?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw a few hundred men on the football field that morning again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened next? Did you continue on towards Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I reached Kladanj with my convoy, and there was the same procedure as the -- as the night before. There was a point where the buses would stop. Everybody had to get out and walk their way on the road towards the Muslim area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did you notice anything particular that day during the disembarkation process?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The buses were more -- were full of people. It wasn't that organised as it was the first convoy. There were -- there were hundreds of people. I don't know. There were 50 or 60 people in the bus the first day, but there were more people standing on every inch of the bus the second day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And once everybody came off the buses, what -- what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported to my OP Alpha, my observation post Alpha that I had to go back again towards the compound, and I reached only as far as Nova Kasaba that day because the other road was closed by Bosnian Serb infantry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happen at that location exactly?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers. They were pointing their guns at us. We had to stop. They took my car and they drove away with the car with all the stuff in it, and I had to sit along with 10 or 12 others on -- on the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And who are these 10 or 12 others you're mentioning?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were Dutch peacekeepers who were on convoy escorting tasks, but they didn't succeed to go past Nova Kasaba. So their cars were taken and they had to wait along the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you see their cars, the UN cars in this area?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time, because they were brought to a school, and because I was a lieutenant at the time, I asked one of the soldiers who was stopping us and face -- and to get in charge of -- to meet with -- with the commanding officer at the time. So I was brought to a school nearby Nova Kasaba. That's where we were stopped. And that's where I met a major, Major Zoran. I always called him by his first name. His last name was Malinic. I've wrote it down so I can look it up if you want to know that. He was in charge of that school. The school was a kind of headquarters for his -- for his group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if we could please display on e-court Prosecutor exhibit, 65 ter number 1688, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the school I've just mentioned. As you can see, nearby the telephone, there's the entrance to the school. This is the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this is seen from what direction?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This from the direction of Kladanj going towards the village of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So when you arrived at the building, who did you go see again? Could you tell us the name again, please?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Major Zoran Malinic. Well, his last name, I got to look it up if you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And could you describe this man, please?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sportive, tall one. He was born in 1961, as I can remember. He had dark black hair with some white colours in it. And he was in charge of the troops who were forming a headquarters inside the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And how did he identify himself to you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was brought to him with an interpreter who spoke excellent English, and I had said, "Well, I'm the highest ranking officer of this group of DutchBat, and I want to meet the commander who was stopping us because we are escorting these convoys, and I have some complaints to -- because of the behaviour of the soldiers." On the road of course they were stopping us, taking our things, threatening us. So I had to make a complaint to him and on his door was his name written as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did he tell you where he was from? Did you have --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he was in charge of more than one battalion, and he was in the neighbour -- in the surroundings of Sarajevo, and he had to go to the Srebrenica area for this operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did he identify himself as being in charge of the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He identified himself as being in charge of the headquarters and the things happening on the road with his soldiers. I was stopped by his soldiers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you know a DutchBat soldier by the name of Mulder?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was with me at that time, and he complained to me that he had to go on an APC, a Dutch APC, a YPR, and he had to go through the woods show -- showing himself as a UN peacekeeper and calling to the Muslims who are in the woods that it's safe for them to come out. And they drove -- there was a Bosnian Serb who was driving the APC. He was on top of the APC screaming to the Muslims that it was safe. And it was this incident and the incident of the stealing of the cars, of the treatment of the UN troops that I had a written complaint taken to this Major Zoran. Those are the stuff that I complained to him about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what did this major say to you about that complaint?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that he was in charge of the headquarters, but he didn't have anything to do with the troops who were along the road all the way to Bratunac, that he had to contact his commanding officer. This commanding officer was named Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: This is what the major said?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what he said, and he tried to get in contact with him so that he could talk to us about the complaint and get us a safe return back to Potocari, because we had a task to fulfil. We had to go with each convoy, UN peacekeepers, on -- or, rather, on the bus we can only follow the convoy. So that was our task, and he couldn't stop us and take our cars, take our stuff, pretend to be a UN peacekeeper and calling the men from the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So at some point in time while you were here, did you or your soldiers try to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said, "Okay, you can go if you want to." So I ordered three UN vehicles to be prepared with peacekeepers, and I ordered them to try to leave the school and go nearby Nova Kasaba and go to Bratunac. And I waited there for other cars who are on the road back towards Nova Kasaba. But unfortunately, one car was coming back, two others were stolen by Bosnian Serbs, and they all walked back for 500 metres with just one car. So it wasn't possible for us to leave the site of the school by our own means and we were not free to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And did the soldiers who returned explain to you what happened?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they told me that there was a gun pointed at them and that they had to leave the car and that the car was taken by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So what did you then decide to do?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I complained about that as well to this major, and he told me that he had to contact Colonel Beara about this and that as soon as he is here at the school he would try to arrange a safe return for us to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And approximately what time of day were you taken to the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The afternoon. So did you spend the night at this school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a -- it was very strange, because -- because I was talking to this major and he invited me for a dinner, and I had to play chess with him. He said, "Well, let's play chess." And he told me about the enclave and -- and the Bosnian Serb point of view about -- about things around -- surrounding the enclave, and he was trying to, well, to -- to get me in a good mood. The soldiers who were with me, they were eating with -- on a special table, and I had to go with him. He was trying to -- to get in contact with this Colonel Beara, and we had to stay the night, and we had a classroom for ourself to stay the night with.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What was this school being used for? Could you tell?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were troops coming in who were having a meal, and there were dogs kept there. There were meals prepared. So it was a kind of headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have discussed something that we consider to be important, particularly since we have arrived to a stage -- or at a stage where the witness is specifically stating that a certain individual pointed out to him that he needed to speak to Colonel Beara. So we need to know with as much precision as possible the identity of this individual the witness was speaking to. Earlier on he said that he could give us his correct or his precise surname if he could check with his notes. So our decision is that he would be given the opportunity to check his notes and give us the exact name and surname of this individual. Of course, with the possibility open to both Prosecution and Defence teams and ourselves to be able to check with this part of his notes. So, Lieutenant Colonel -- yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact there is a document, a report that Lieutenant Colonel Egbers himself had written at the time or shortly after returning from Nova Kasaba, which was I was going to be bringing up. If you would like, I can do so at this time and he can from this very report identify and look at the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but with this proviso, that if he still needs to check his notes to make sure that the name and surname are correct, then we will give him all the opportunity. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Even though it's nice and we are thankful for our -- the Prosecutor for helping out here, but we'd like to see his notes, and I didn't realise he had notes, and if he can be -- if we can get those notes that would really help us. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, but that will not be the case, not unless he's referring to his notes. And what I mentioned was refer only to that part of his notes where he has specific reference to the name and surname of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand now and then I would object to the Prosecutor showing him -- showing him her documents that she believes may or may not have that name, and I would rather that we have him look at his notes and maybe the Court can have an in camera inspection. But I didn't realise he had notes, and I think it's only fair to give our client a fair trial and for justice to be followed that the notes be produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's out of the question at the moment, Mr. Ostojic. Let's make ourselves clear, if you are thinking that as a follow-up to what we stated you pretend to be entitled to go through his entire notes, you're far off what we had intended. What we had intended is this: The witness said if you want the precise name, I need to consult my notes. He will be given the opportunity to consult that particular part of his notes where he knows that is what the precise name and surname, and it's only that page or whatever it is that we will allow you to -- the Prosecution and ourselves to see. Otherwise until and unless he is making use of the entire notes that he has for the purpose of his testimony, we will -- we will not force him to hand us or to show you or anyone else for that matter his notes. So the position, I think, we'd like to do it both ways. You will make use of that document because it's a report which you allege has been drawn up by the witness himself, so you are perfectly entitled to make use of that document and ask him a question. We would still prefer to make sure that he first checks with his notes to ensure -- and make sure that he is now hundred per cent familiar with the name and surname of this person. So, Lieutenant Colonel, you can check your note or your notes. Don't tell us you don't have them here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, can I explain something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I didn't bring anything out of the enclave except the things I have typed out and are in the dossier of this case. So right -- when I was in the enclave, I used the computer and I wrote everything down on paper, and that's what's inside of -- so I don't have a book with -- with my notes. It's all typed out, and I handed it over. So when I can have a look at that piece of paper, I can. I'm sure that they've got the same papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have -- has what Lieutenant Colonel's referring to been disclosed to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So then let's proceed. I think it becomes very simplified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was acting under a misunderstanding. Obviously I thought that he had some notes that he had brought with him, presumably that he was going to show us, but it's not the case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for the misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So if we can just make a final clarification. Upon your return to Potocari in July 1995, you typed up a report, did you not?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this report was typed up in the Dutch language; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And we indeed have it here. Now, I have the Dutch version here, but we have of course provided the Defence with both the B/C/S and the English versions of it. I can give you the ERN number, and the ERN number for this is R013-5633 to R013-5636. Now, for the purposes of refreshing the recollection of Lieutenant Colonel Egbers, I don't know whether you -- whether it would be wiser to give him the actual original Dutch language notes for him to take a look at. I have a copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: See what he prefers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I have a copy here with me, and then of course we can also put that on the ELMO or e-court, however you would like that. And the specific pages that he's looking at of this report are RO135635 to RO0135636.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you have a chance -- do you need to focus it a little more, please. I think the English version needs to be focused a little better. We're almost getting there. Now, perhaps if I could have the Lieutenant Colonel Egbers read into the record the particular --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- paragraph or paragraphs which deal with the identification of this individual.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I spoke about Major Zoran Malinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And could you read, please, for us the particular paragraph in which you wrote his name.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was number 5. "I asked to speak to the local commander who was in a former school building which had been converted into a temporary barracks, Major Zoran Milanic, born 1961, and told him that the convoys were being escorted at the orders of Major General Mladic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I distinctly heard the witness pronounce "Major Zoran Milanic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Malinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But what we have written here is Malinic [sic]. I just want to make sure that it is Malinic and not Milanic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You had said that you had spent -- you spent the evening at the headquarters with this major?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And where were your Dutch -- the other Dutch soldiers who were there? Where were they at this time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were inside the school, and they -- we slept there that night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What was the atmosphere like during the night? Was there anything in particular that you could note about --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the night there was a lot of firing in -- in the neighbourhood of the -- of the school, and it was a firing, not a combat of -- there was just a lot of machine-gun firing. And as I -- as I asked this Major Malinic about it, he said, "Well, we've got young troops and when there is some sound they will all just fire at the woods." That's what he said to me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take you back just a moment to the afternoon, to the evening that you spent at the school. During your time there, close to the -- the road to Nova Kasaba, did you notice any other convoys?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only thing we could do at that time because all the escorts were stopped at the school was to go towards the road and to count all the buses with women and children who were coming by. So I saw at that time a lot of buses going towards Kladanj but no escort on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have a number of the buses? Did you yourself count a number?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I didn't do that myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had some radio contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With OP Alpha.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I believe this might be a time for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan, can I hear from the witness the time frame what happened to Mr. Mulder happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Of course. Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So Lieutenant Colonel, if you could just tell us briefly, did lieutenant -- did Sergeant Mulder tell you exactly when the events he complained about happened to him?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on that morning that it happened to him. So we were escorting all the -- all the buses, and in the morning he had to go on an APC that was given by Bosnian Serbs. He was taken inside the -- through the woods, and he had to call for Muslims that it was safe for them to come out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did he tell you how long that lasted from the moment he was --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell me, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we break, I forgot to mention one thing in relation to our decision on the video that -- pronounced earlier on. We also took notice of what Madam Fauveau and others had mentioned. I mean, the practice should be that any such document, even if it is intended or earmarked or of interest to one of the accused only, it should be disclosed to all others, because I don't think there should be any distinctions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Apparently it was actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am told by Madam Fauveau, Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Haynes, and Mr. Bourgon that it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Very briefly -- very briefly. The document that is now on the ELMO appears somewhat different from the document I have that was disclosed to us. There is very minor changes on those first few paragraphs. I would just like permission to see this document on the ELMO just to compare the two. There is some editing that's been done between -- Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's an interesting matter that you've raised.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, just one more quick thing. I misunderstood you. Indeed we disclosed this document. The video has been disclosed to all the parties in 2006. On our 65 -- well, in fact, it was disclosed on December 19 of 2005 to all the parties, and then was in fact marked on the 65 ter exhibit list as the -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The new one. The one that has been -- this is what was intended.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The new one is -- as far as I know is very new and that is coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but it was shown to --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, you'll discuss this amongst yourselves, please, and the message is what is of interest to one party may be of interest to all the others and should be -- should --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I just may for the record just state, the video that -- the new video that they received, according to Mr. McCloskey yesterday, he told me he got it several months ago. That was never disclosed to us. He had it several months ago. He didn't get it yesterday, a week ago, a month ago. And we insisted, and we said, "Did you get it before or after the trial?" He said, "I had it several months ago." But I just wanted to put that on the record. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're getting to the point where we'll be playing the tape soon. I have had a chance to see the tape as it goes through the audio booth and comes out on our screens and as you know we have computer screens, and so the television screen gives a much better picture than the computer screens. So when we show him the tape, the tape will not have as much quality on it through this system, and I -- I can compare the two and even I can tell you that they're degraded. So we have brought in the TV and that can be played, if you would like it to. If think once you see the computer thing you're going to want to see what he saw, and we have it here. Now, I've now figured out what the complaints the Defence have, and they're right. We did not show the other Defence counsel this tape, and we didn't tell them last night that -- that we had decided we needed to play it, and we should have. It was late and we didn't get to that, and we always try to make sure we tell everybody everything, but that's a fair criticism. But just back to the other issue. We can play the tape through the system and, if you'd like, then you can see it or Defence can see it roughly the way the witness would have seen it when he was shown it. So I just wanted to give you those options so you could decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, or anyone else for that matter, do you wish to contribute to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We would just defer to your better judgement, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My -- if you don't agree with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think the best -- we think that the best way to proceed about it is that you, Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Soljan, you are best positioned to know what is closest to what he was shown when he was interviewed by the investigators of -- or officers of the OTP, and then we'll take it up from there. If it's what you intend to show us on this TV screen that you think was shown to him, then we'll proceed along those lines, and of course there will be all the opportunities for the Defence to ask questions. And then we see whatever else there is to see if it is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's a little awkward because we have to recreate the investigative situation and there it is. And we can play it over to the witness, then we can play it to you, then we can play it to counsel. It's really only 10 seconds or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and we can actually focus -- focus a camera -- focus a camera on it and we see what comes out. I mean, it's -- I don't want to predict or anticipate anything, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'll go take my seat in the back and see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll see. But it needs to -- how are we going to get the witness to come here and watch it from here? Or can it be moved to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If audiovisual can help us, that we can move it close to the witness, that would probably be the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the way it should be done, Mr. McCloskey, is that it should be placed as near the witness as possible, also in a way which is visible particularly to Mr. Ostojic, and at the same time if one of the cameras can focus on it while this is being shown, I think it will give the opportunity to everyone and then we'll see it ourselves later, or any one of the Defence teams who wishes to see it again. I mean, it's a short clip. Okay. Okay. That should -- should be enough. All right. And one of the cameras will focus on it while we proceed. How long is it, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: About six to 10 seconds is all, and it's going to be -- you're going to want to see it a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As the witness will testify he did when he saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Let's bring the witness in. Mr. Ostojic, please don't ask him whether he's seen that television before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Lieutenant Colonel, we are going to show you an a very short footage, and not immediately. Oh, I see. Yes, okay. All right. We'll come to it. I thought it was going to be shown immediately. Go ahead, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It will be becoming very shortly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, you were telling us about the night that you spent at the school in Nova Kasaba, and you had mentioned that you were -- you heard firing happen during the night. Could you tell what kind of weapons were being used?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was automatic fire by machine-guns, and it was in the -- environs the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you tell what direction the fire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it -- we thought -- I thought it was in the direction of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, while you were at the school, did you have the opportunity to walk around the grounds?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were able to -- to sit inside the school and the playing grounds, in the environs of the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
