utterances.text: And could you please describe for us your observations outside the grounds in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a house -- well, let's say there was a room where they kept Muslims, boys and men, inside. It was on the road from the -- from the road to the school that there was a small, let's say chambers. I don't know whether it's a real house, but that's where they kept the men that were brought by the -- by the road towards this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And how many men where in this building?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, let's say, 20 or 30 men and boys.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How did they look?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one had a black -- a blue eye. He was -- and another one had a stomach of -- who had injuries at his belly, and they were all there with just a bucket to stay in there for the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And when did you observe these men in this room?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We observed them the first day in the afternoon and the second day I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in the course of the second day, can you describe us how that -- how that morning progressed? Just tell us.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the privates who was with me at the school managed to get a friendly relationship with one of the Bosnian Serbs who was there at the school, and because we heard firing that night we wanted to check whether those men who were inside this building were still alive. So he said -- well, this private who was a Dutch soldier, he said well, we can -- "I've arranged that we can have a look." So I joined him, and together we had a look at the men who were there. They were there still alive, and two of them were very -- were injured at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And during the morning was there any continued shooting?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no shooting at the sites. The night -- it happened that night, but we were shot by, I think, Muslim fire at that time. There were a few rounds hit inside the school. So this major, he fired every -- every weapon he had on the grounds in front of the school, and then he took two boys outside of the house I just described. He used them as a shield, and he tried to fight the two -- fight the men who were -- who fired at the school at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: When you say "boys," how old did these individuals look to be?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were 16. I think some could be 14 or 18, but they were very young.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after a half an hour they came back, and those boys were put back into the -- into the room with the others, and he said that he didn't -- he couldn't see the men who were firing at the school at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: When was this approximately? What time of day?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened next; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, next apparently Mr. -- Colonel Beara appeared at the school, and I knew this because the interpreter who was typing out these complaints in Bosnian Serb and in English told me that he would arrive and that I could meet him, and I -- I went to the parking place and there was a luxurious car coming, not an army car or something like that, just a normal car, and there was Colonel Beara, and I saluted him. I said who I was, and I handed out the complaints about the APC, the written complaints about the cars that had been stolen from us, the -- the bullet-proof vest. I've mentioned him that there was an APC, a Dutch APC, with Serbs in it who were just acting to be UN peacekeepers by wearing our clothes and using our vehicles. And I asked him to guide us back to the compound, not to take us -- to leave us at the school any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Were you using the interpreter at that time when you were speaking to this colonel?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke to him, I spoke in English and it was all translated by this interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe for us what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I described him in one of my debriefing reports as a tall man with grey hair but with an atmosphere of a colonel. He was in a camouflage suit wearing a colonel's ranking. So that's how I remember him, as a big, giant colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, sir, you've given a few statements to the ICTY in the past describing Colonel Beara; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you remember having a meeting in April 30, 2000 with two investigators?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do -- I do remember that, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember at this meeting having the opportunity to watch a short video?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen a short video that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for us what was on that video, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was six years ago, but I'm sure that there was a celebration, an inspection of troops by General Mladic and by a giant colonel with grey hair, who might have been Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, we will play a video for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: If we could have the video unit start this. Okay. And this is, for the record, 65 ter 2025.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to note our same objection, Your Honour, just for the record, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- have you seen this video before?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So this is --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the video I saw, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you recall approximately how many times you may have looked at it or have seen it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, do you need to see it one more time or was the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Pause. Maybe go a few seconds. Could you pause, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the individual?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the individual who is behind General Mladic as the Colonel Beara I saw in 1995 at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. So, Lieutenant Colonel, you said you spoke to Colonel Beara at that time. How long was your conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a short conversation. He didn't say much. He just took the written complaint, and he went to this major inside the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you see him talk to the major at the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there when he talked to this major.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And just for clarifications purposes, when you refer to "this major," it is the major that we had identified earlier as Major Zoran Malinic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What happened next after Colonel Beara went to speak to the major?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we -- this Major Zoran Malinic arranged our safe return towards Srebrenica, the compound of the UN. We left the two cars we had, and we took place in a BOV. That's an Armed Personnel Carrier by the -- by the Serbs, by the Bosnian Serbs. And he drove us all the way back towards the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How soon after major -- after Colonel Beara's visit did you leave for Potocari or were you escorted to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been a few hours. So in the night I think it was 9.00 that we did arrive at -- at the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did Colonel Beara stay at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Colonel left after he talked to the major at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How long would you say he stayed at the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he only stayed for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you see him leave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened with your written complaint?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I gave it to the Colonel Beara, and he took it with him to Major Zoran, but I never saw it again. And I had a copy of it and a copy of the complaint written in English and in Serbo-Croatian was given to me by -- or to the operations section of the battalion of DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you yourself keep a copy of that complaint?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And do you know where a copy of complaint could be found?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was burnt when we left the enclave or that it was taken to Zagreb. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. But at the time that you were at the school in Nova Kasaba, was any immediate action taken on this complaint?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only action that was taken was that we would be brought back safely to the compound, and at that time there were no escorts. There were no buses to be escorted to Kladanj. That was all over. So there -- there was something done by the safety of -- of the Dutch troops. And the only thing we did was complaining about the UN APC be used by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. How were you transported back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was inside of the BOV, as I call it, and when I was driving back towards the compound, I saw, but I didn't have a clear vision, I saw a dead Muslim with -- with a rucksack on his back lying dead on the -- dead on the road, and the driver, he was making jokes and he was trying not to hit the body. I saw goods of the men who were inside -- or nearby the road burning, so it was -- and then of course there was a lot of infantry standing there near the road, but there was of course no stopping of those vehicles and they brought us safely back. They even gave me some presents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: To clarify this, you mentioned a BOV. Could you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A BOV is an Armed Personnel Carrier by the -- used by the Bosnian Serbs with a machine-gun on top of it, and you can transport troops in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. So how many of you were in this BOV, of the Dutch -- DutchBat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we drove back in two BOVs, so the group was divided in two, and we were with six or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what route did you take in order to get back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back the normal route we came to, so via Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. The same route that you had taken --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same route, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you again pass that football field in Nova Kasaba on your way?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. But I don't have any recollection of -- of the men who are in or on the football field. Because I was inside the BOV, I didn't have a clear view, and it was -- the night was falling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: You mentioned, however, that you saw a dead body, a dead man, with a rucksack on his back in the road in the road. What kind of -- does a BOV have windows?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting in the front, so I could watch outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So was your vision of this body relatively clear?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you tell the age of this man?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- it was an older man. I didn't know how old he was, but he was older.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And did you make any other significant observations along your route back to Potocari that you can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can tell you is that there was goods burning in -- nearby the road, that there were infantry, Bosnian Serb infantry were still there and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And to clarify for the Court when you're talking about goods burning, what specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw a lot of personal belongings like rucksacks and backs but they were all together and burning. But it wasn't a place where, let's say, rucksacks and bags are all together and then set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. When did you arrive back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, next I reported everything I saw to the operation of -- the operations section of DutchBat. I typed my report, and I've waited for permission to go back to Zagreb with -- with the rest of the battalion. I didn't leave the enclave at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And you left when, the compound?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all left at July 24th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are now going to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise to you. We are going to proceed now with the various cross-examinations. Have you determined who is going first this time? I suppose Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'd like to go first, and it's by agreement of my colleagues and I appreciate that. With your permission, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Ostojic is appearing for Colonel Beara who is an accused in this trial. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Egbers, good morning, how are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you a series of questions, and I think although I have an outline I'd like to first go with a description of an individual that you met in July of 1995, if you will. Is your recollection of the events that occurred in 1995 still fresh in your mind?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on what -- on what, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll break it down, thank you. How about your meeting with Mr. -- or Major Zoran Malinic? Is that fresh in your mind?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And as you sit here, sir, you remember what he looks like; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's fresh in your mind today?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen him for 11 years, but I have described him as a major with black hair, with some grey or white pieces of hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you never said grey, but I'll accept that if you want to modify it, with black hair?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, on page 29, line -- 19 through 21 of your testimony, you described Major Zoran Malinic as having dark black hair with white colour. As you sit here, did he have grey or was it just white or you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I thought it was white, but it could as also be grey because man born in 1961 could have grey hair in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was specific. I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you wrote it down where, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write it down at that time in notes, but shortly after that I was debriefed six weeks after I left the enclave, and then it was written down by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive me for asking, but blonde is not black; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, I want to make sure we have the same terminology. Blonde is almost like a yellowish colour; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you described Major Zoran Malinic you described him as being tall. Would you estimate -- can you estimate for us how tall you believe he was?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not as tall as you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's pretty obvious maybe, right? But thank you for that. Was he taller or shorter than you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the same length, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how tall are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do it in metres. 188.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. Now, you also mentioned that you met General Mladic during your tenure while you were serving for DutchBat III in Srebrenica and Potocari. Can you tell us how tall General Mladic is?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's shorter than you and shorter than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well -- and how much shorter is he than you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other things to focus on at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's shorter, and I think he's approximately 20 or 30 centimetres shorter than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that would make him what then, 158, or 168?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. Next question, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you first -- you gave three reports to the Office of the Prosecutor: One in 1995, as I recall; one in 1999; and then one again in 2000. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember the 1995 report I wrote myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's the report that was closest to the time frame or the events that occurred because it was in 1995, the events that we're discussing; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can tell you in your report dated October 24, 1995, with the Office of the Prosecutor, you described Mr. Malinic, and I will get that for you and cite it to the Court for the record and to the Prosecutor. And if they can look at ERN number 00443212, which is page 6 of that report. And with the Court's permission -- and with the Court's permission, that's dated October 24, 1995. Let me read it first and I'll invite you to look at it on the ELMO in a second. You described Mr. Major Malinic and you described him as follows --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, could the counsel say the number in e-court, 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's 2D00019. But I'd like to ask him first before we show him, but we could do it that way. Whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it should be done simultaneously, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And if we could have the usher please place the first page on the report so he can identify it and then the last page, and then I'll ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's how we should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Egbers, do you see the first page of the report?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the first page of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it has your name on it, correct, with the date that I just referenced, the 24th of October, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now if we can direct your attention to the last page of the report, please. It doesn't seem to have a signature page. Did you ever sign the report?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not -- it's not signed, so I didn't sign this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know why you didn't sign it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that it's signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But there's no signature, though, but ...

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't sign the translation in English, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You signed the Dutch version?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now if I can -- how sure are you of your description of Major Zoran Malinic as having dark hair with some white?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure when I wrote the report and I was asked about it. I told them how I thought he had his hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he had any curls? Like curly hair?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know the person but they have to type it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, did you tell them if he had curls or not?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Black curls or white curls?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me direct your attention to page 6 of your report, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if we could enlarge the first paragraph that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to focus on the fifth line down, sir. It starts basically: "He was dressed --" do you notice that we're talking about Zoran Malinic born in 1961? Do you see that on the fourth line?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then the text proceeds to state as follows: "He was dressed in camouflage uniform and had no insignia distinguishing his rank." Who are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about Major Zoran Malinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I thought. Thank you. You proceed to state: "He was about 1.85 metres tall." We're still talking about Major Malinic; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are still.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Next one. "He had grey hair with blonde curls." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are we still talking about Major Zoran Malinic?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are still talking about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, as I asked you earlier, your description on page 29 of Mr. Zoran -- or Major Malinic, lines 19 through 21, was that he had dark black hair with white colour. In your report of the 24th of October, 1995, you describe him as having "grey hair with blonde curls." Could you, sir, reconcile that for me? How do you go from black to blonde, or from white to grey?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I recall him, and I can imagine him because it was on a very hot day in 1995, that day I never forget, that he had black hair. So it says here that he had grey hair, but it should have been black at that time with some grey or white in it. So he didn't change. He didn't change in my memory. You're correct that it says grey hair. And I've always talked about black hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it talks about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Can the witness be shown the original statement in Dutch, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't have it immediately here but we'll call up for it and have it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it exist in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you could please make it available.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We would like a copy if at all possible also. We never did receive that one. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned that's basically the same person with the same description, although somewhat different; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still talking about Major Zoran Malinic who I met in 1995 and described him as a man as tall as I am with -- with grey -- with dark hair. What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think I understand where you're coming from. Sir, Ms. Soljan asked you questions about whether you heard certain firings during approximately the 12th through the 14th of July, 1995. Do you remember when she asked you about that, whether you heard shots? And then she asked you to describe what type of gunfire you would have -- I don't want to say speculated or guessed, but what you thought was being used. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now before that July 12th or 13th period, did you suffer any injuries to your body?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was shelled when I was at blocking position Bravo 1, and there were mortars fired on, let's say, 20 or 30 metres from me, so at that time I've had a beep in my ear for -- for the entire day, but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what time period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was at Bravo 1, we were shelled by the Bosnian Serbs, and then I had a small injury at my ear for, let's say, the entire day, because there was an explosion nearby. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to any injury you may have suffered, sir. Is that the only injury you suffered?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The ear?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only injury I've had.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a few days before that. That was on the 9th or 10th of July. But it's in my testimony. I'm sure you looked it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having that confidence if me. I appreciate that. Sir, when you talk about shelling and all that, isn't it true that on July 8th it was the Muslim fighters who had thrown hand-grenades between your vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how often did the Muslim fighters throw hand-grenades at your vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were -- that was only that day at that time that the Muslim fighters tried to keep us there and threw a grenade at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many times that day did they throw the grenade at you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can recall, it's only that day that the Muslim fighters threw a hand-grenade at the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that would be one time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was one time, but I don't know whether it was one or two grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought in your statement of the 24th of October you state plural, grenades. Would you like to read it through to refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that before or after you'd turned back to Bravo Company?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The throwing of the grenades was at the first day, the day of the 8th, in the evening when I had to go south in the enclave. Then the grenades were thrown, and I got back to the headquarters of the Bravo Company, and then I've got to go to Bravo 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So after the grenades were thrown, you returned back to Bravo Company; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, describe for us, if you will, sir, what those Muslim fighters who threw the grenades at you or at your vehicles, what they were dressed like.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen Muslim fighters in the south of the enclave. Some were -- some were -- had Ukraine uniforms on. Others were just in civilian clothes. They were having RPG-7 with them and a machine-gun, so they were armed at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about AK-47s? Were they armed with that as well?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, according to your statement, the following day you were asked to proceed to support other vehicles in Srebrenica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that accurate, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall if at that time, the next day when you were ordered to support other vehicles in Srebrenica, whether Muslim fighters started shooting at you at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I was -- the APCs were shot by AK-47s at that time, and I had -- one soldier had a light injury at his arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the type of weapons that the Muslim fighters had on that next day, July 9th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a piece of artillery. I thought it was a Mike 48 because I've looked it up in 1995. A piece of artillery hidden in the exact position where we had Bravo 1. So it was a few metres from us away. Let's say 40, 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anything other than that piece of artillery? Is it Mike 48?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it's a Mike 48. That's what I thought it was. And I asked the Muslim fighters not to fire the gun because we were in the neighbourhood. And it didn't fire, but it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What other types of weapons did you see the Muslim fighters having on July 9th, 1995, other than this artillery, piece of artillery Mike 48?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw the RPG-7. I saw the machine-gun and the AK-47.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, was there anything significant that happened on July 9, 1995, that you recall as you sit here, such as other units or other DutchBat personnel being attacked in other areas by Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the only attack we had was by leaving an observation post in the south of the enclave where one of our soldiers got killed. Do you -- do you point at that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't. Because I think that happened the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So we're already past the 8th of July and we're now on the 9th of July, the second attack by the Muslim fighters. And I'm asking you other than the attack that occurred with you, did you have any information that any other units on July 9, 1995, were being attacked by Muslim fighters in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall ever discussing with Captain Hageman whether or not he was under fire and under attack by Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined captain -- this captain at the marketplace in Srebrenica, and when I was there there was no firing at us. There were Muslim fighters with the weapons I just described. They were aiming at us, so they wanted us -- them -- they wanted us to stay at the marketplace, but they didn't fire at us at that time. And I don't know whether Captain Hageman was -- was under Muslim fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can have 2D19, placed on the e-court screen again, please. And I'd like -- and Lieutenant Colonel, it's the same document that we've looked at previously, just so you know. I'm going to turn to page 3 of that document, if I may. And directing your attention, if I may, to the second paragraph which starts with: "We took up our position about 400 metres further on." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said -- yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Several sentences below that - I'm just directing your attention sir, thank you - it says: "I then received the order to support the four other vehicles in Srebrenica. We left our position and the Muslim fighters started shooting at us." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then the next paragraph you describe that -- do you see when it starts "In Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It states: " ... I saw many armed Muslims ..." And then you describe the weapons that they had. My question at this point, sir, is: When you say "many," how many do you mean, or how many did you see, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I think there were 50 or 60 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The following sentence - again I'm directing your attention - is on the fourth line. It states as follows: "We drove to another four vehicles which belonged to us and we were under the command of Captain Hageman." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And it's the same captain we were just discussing; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Am I pronouncing his name incorrectly, is that why you're smiling?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You proceed to state on this document that you signed: "He told me over the radio," and I'll stop there. Who are we referring to when it says "he"?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must be Captain Hageman.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just proceed. "He told me over the radio that he was under fire by the local Muslim fighters and therefore he could not move his vehicles." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that, sir, refresh your recollection that in fact other units of DutchBat other than yourself on the 9th of July, 1995, were under attack?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you before, he was on the marketplace with his vehicles and he radioed me, as I read it, that he had -- he had some fire on his APC, but not when I was there, and not on my APC at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair. But as you sit here now, you now recall that you had this radio teleconference with Captain Hageman and he informed you he was under attack by the Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall it because it was not that very important to me. But I wrote it down, I'm sure about that, that this is signed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it's accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I -- as I recall. I don't think about -- I didn't have a clear view about Captain Hageman's position at that time. I can only tell you about what happened to me, and I don't know whether he was under attack. I wrote it down because that's what he told me on the radio, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Sir, during those two days when DutchBat was under attack by various Muslim fighters, can you explain to us if you know why they were under attack by Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that we were under attack by Muslim fighters. I can only tell you about what happened to me. When I left Bravo 1 to join the -- the other APCs who are on the marketplace, there was AK-47 fire to my APC, and I'm sure that there was fire because they were sure that we would abandon them, and we couldn't tell them that we were leaving for the marketplace in Srebrenica town to -- to help out there. So their reaction was -- were a few rounds of fire to the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A few rounds that Captain Hageman couldn't even leave; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you about what happened to me at Bravo 1. Captain Hageman was on the marketplace in Srebrenica town. That was his experience. But you don't have to fire at APCs to make sure that -- that they don't leave. Just threatening is enough, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, share with me, sir, where you state on page 67, line 4, or 5 -- 3 through 4 "because they were sure that we would abandon them." Who did you talk to specifically that you obtained that information from?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I contacted the -- the group of Muslim who were nearby the piece of artillery, and I tried to arrange that they wouldn't fire the piece of artillery because we were in the neighbourhood. What he did was he wrote down a note to his commanding officer who was in I guess Srebrenica or Potocari, and until that time he didn't use the gun or the piece of artillery. So he -- we tried to -- to get in contact with them, with those 10 men who were surrounding the -- the piece of artillery. He was writing a note. The note went down to the -- I think the man who was in charge of them, and during that time we had -- we had contact. So that was the group. And we tried to have a good relationship, not to, of course, to fire at each other. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But your DutchBat tried to have that good relationship with both sides, the Serbs and the Muslims. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, now, did you make a report as to the person that you talked to on the Muslim side that was actually shooting or threatening to shoot you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I did was to radio it to the Bravo Company, the Captain Groen who was in command of the Bravo Company, and he wrote everything down. I didn't make a report at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the individual that you spoke to, what was his rank?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you can -- you can -- you can have a rank on -- on this man because he was just a civilian with a weapon. He didn't have a -- they didn't wear uniforms. They were just there. Some had a weapon, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what did they do with the Ukrainian uniforms, just carry them in a bag or over their arm? I thought you had described earlier for me that they were dressed in camouflage and had Ukrainian uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I talked about the Ukrainian uniforms, it was worn by men who were in the south of the enclave. They were not nearby Bravo 1. And it's not so. The picture is there were a few men who would wear these uniforms, but it's a small person -- a small persons of the group, just a few men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many men were there? I know on the first day, on the 8th of July, you had estimated there were approximately 60 men; correct? And now on the 9th of July how much would your estimate be?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any observations in the south of the enclave at that time. The only thing I saw was the 10 men who were -- who were nearby Bravo 1 with this piece of artillery we called Mike 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting Mr. Ostojic, but we just received the Dutch translation or the original of the 24th October, 1995, statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If is it convenient for both of you, or for you in particular, Mr. Ostojic, perhaps we can go back to that paragraph where he describes Malinic's hair again and see how it's written in the Dutch language. I think it was page -- page 6 in the English version. I wouldn't know what page it is in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I could give one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will as soon as they're distributed, Your Honour, or whatever you'd like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Just give him a chance to do that. Yes, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to go back on the record, Your Honour, if I may, just so that the record is somewhat clear. The witness has been given a copy of what purports to be the 24th of October, 1995, statement that he gave to the ICTY in his language, which is Dutch, and he will direct us to the page when he finds it. If I can direct the witness to page 6 of that document, which has ERN number 00353520, and it's the second full paragraph -- or third full paragraph, I'm sorry, and it's mid -- mid-paragraph on that third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And please, Mr. Lieutenant Colonel Egbers, just let me know when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it in the Dutch language, and it said that he had grey hair. It said -- let's see. He had grey hair. I see "grey" over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he does, and it says there, and we could maybe make it out, but doesn't he also use the word "blonde" right next to that word or in the next sentence?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm emphasising, as I'm sure you know. It says blonde what? Blonde locks, right --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- in your language, or blonde curls as it may be translated. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's a good translation of the locks. In Dutch it says "blonde locks," but I refer when I see him in my mind I see a man with black hair with some grey or blonde pieces of hair. It was very particular because I haven't seen it before. And I'm sure that you've got a photograph of this man for us now to see how he really looks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court has any other questions on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, no. It's just to make sure what -- because he said earlier on that he had drawn up this himself, so we now have it in the Dutch language, and we --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's why I'm just checking if the Court had anything else. I would move on from this section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We intervene as little as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And we will get to some photographs later hopefully a little later, Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But right now I'm going to focus back on July 10, 1995, as we just discussed July 8, 9, so the next day we'd like to discuss is July 10. Do you recall, sir, when the F-16 bombed Serb military in Srebrenica or around that area?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what date was that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the last day that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what day --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Bravo 1. I don't have all -- it was on the fourth day, so it was 8, 9, 10, 11th. July 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was on July 11. After the -- strike that. Do you know how many tanks, if any, those F-16s that shot at the Serb military, how many tanks they took out, if any?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that there was one tank who was between us and the town of Srebrenica, and that it didn't move, it didn't fire at us after the attack. That's the often thing -- I didn't have a clear view on the tank itself. I don't know whether it was hit or it was -- I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, after that date do you know if the evacuation of the people in Potocari began?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the same day but a day later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, when the Muslim male column, military column was moving towards the north-westernly direction from the area of Srebrenica approximately?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know what happened in the north of the enclave. I wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So as you sit here today, you don't know if they left on the 8th, 9th or any time thereafter; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at Bravo 1 at that time. Later on I was at Srebrenica and Potocari, and I wasn't at the observation post or nearby where the men get out to get out of the enclave. So I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recall obtaining orders from your commander? Was Lieutenant Colonel Franken one of your commanders? He was the second man in charge, correct, of DutchBat III?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the second man in command, but at the time I was at Bravo 1 I was under the command of Captain Groen, and he was the one who had contact with this Major Franken.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thank you for that. So you never had any contact directly with Major Franken; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a day later on when I had to escort the first convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was the 13th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Must be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Did you ever hear from your immediate commander or from Major Franken whether or not he received a verbal order to assist in the evacuation of the people in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've talked about this with Major Franken. He told me that he wanted to have a DutchBat soldier on every bus, that he tried to negotiate that, but the only thing he had approval of was a vehicle escorting the buses. So that's the only thing I can say about that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay, don't be sorry. If it's your best recollection, we'll accept it. So you don't know what, if any, order Major Franken received to cooperate or to support the evacuation of the refugees; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he has to support the evacuation. The only thing I knew was that it was very hot, there was no water left, and it was the only thing we could do was join the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that he's probably the best one that would be able to tell us if he was to support the evacuation; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, I'd like to discuss with you briefly the topic of -- that you mentioned in your direct examination today. You mention when you weapon this first convoy was approximately when, the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure you've looked it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have but I'm not testifying. So if you don't know, I'll help you but --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Help me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I thought you said the 12th of July, 1995. But whatever date it is we'll accept it, okay? It's the first time you took convoy.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And approximately 14 buses; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 to 14, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 12 to 14. Do you remember telling the Prosecutor that you were in the -- towards the end or the very end of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you have at that time radio equipment with you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact I think you shared with us that you radioed back to inform your commander or your commanding officers what exactly you saw or transpired during that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, at one point you testified that you didn't know where the buses or convoys were going. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who was in the front of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the front of the convoy was another vehicle, were two DutchBat officers were in, Major Boering and a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if Major Boering and a captain were leading the convoy and you were behind the convoy, how could you not know where the convoy was going? Couldn't you have radioed Major Boering to find out?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't at that time know whether he had the same radio contact with my observation post, because as I started my testimony, you know I was in charge of observation post Alpha, and I always had contact with observation post Alpha. But nobody told us where the buses would go to. We just had to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, did you call him and ask him where he was going since he was in the lead vehicle on this convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't the one with -- he wasn't the one in front of the convoy and everybody following him. That was not -- that was not the case at that time. He was in -- he was forward. He wasn't the one who say, "Follow me, I know where to go to." He was in the front of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not having talked to him as I thought you said, how do you know that he didn't know or that he was not in the front of the convoy? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because we were told that we had to take everything we needed as water, food, sleeping bags. We didn't know where to go to. We just had to follow the buses. But nobody told me that they would go to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I understand your testimony, I apologise, but -- so is it your testimony that Colonel Boering was not in the front leading the convoy but he was somewhere towards the front of this 14- or 12-bus convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just tell me what you think it is.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just wait once she's typed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just made a picture of following the car of Major Boering, so "Follow me, I know where to go," but we didn't know where the buses were going to. And I was on the -- I was nearby the last bus to leave the enclave and that's where I was, and I was always in contact with OP Alpha. So I don't know whether this Major Boering knew anything else than I did, but I didn't know that, and I radioed that towards OP Alpha.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now during this trip, how long did it take you to get to your ultimate destination?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was over an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you delayed for any reason during this first convoy trip that you made on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, one bus broke down and the bus was on side of the road and I stopped with the bus. So the other buses, they drove on, and I stopped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it that time, sir, that you stopped at that bus that you obtain the assistance of a new bus or a bus that already had other people being evacuated that you helped load on? I'm unclear with your statements really about that.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time whether the bus stopped I took everybody out of the bus, and the driver asked me whether he could use my vehicle to get another bus, but I didn't -- I didn't do that. I just kept my -- my own vehicle and my own stuff with me at that time and another bus got arranged at that time, but it wasn't an empty bus. It was -- it was coming back from Kladanj. It was a new bus. I don't know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought you just said it came from Kladanj. You don't know where it came from, or you do?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was an empty bus coming from Kladanj that we could use again. So it was a bus but it could have been from Zvornik as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. The next day you also escorted a convoy of people evacuated towards the same route; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you also at that time, sir, experience a delay or something that would cause you to interrupt your complete and -- trip to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What happened on that second day? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't testify about that yet, but there was another bus broke down; it was on the way from Milici to Kladanj. And there was a colonel in a black uniform with yellow ranking who -- who helped to get another bus, and that might have been a bus coming from Kladanj. I can't recall that. And that all the people could get into that bus and proceed to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm ultra-sensitive when you mention "colonel." But in fact you had met -- this is the first time that you met some other colonel. It's not Colonel Beara that you recall; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe this colonel in black uniform with a yellow insignia, please?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't describe him better than what I have just done, but it was a colonel wearing a black uniform wearing a yellow rank on his chest, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What did the rank state?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What did the rank state.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was -- at that time I believed it was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were there other people with him?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three people with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how long did you spend time with him there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, within those five minutes, sir, were you able to communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you -- not other than just this bus broke down, can you arrange one, and he did it within five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how did you communicate to him that he would be able to arrange a bus for you? Did you have an interpreter or did you -- sign language again, maybe?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only had to point out the bus -- the bus broke down and that -- you know, it's not a very difficult situation to explain what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that it is.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. So I just pointed at the bus and I wanted another bus and that's what he arranged. And the only thing I know now and I knew then that it was -- he was in a black uniform. That was extraordinary. I couldn't recall his face; I've seen him for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what type of car or vehicle he was driving?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- he drove in a luxurious car. It wasn't a military car at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say "luxurious," what does that mean? Is that like an Opel Omega?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's like an Omega, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have that kind of car, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got to look it up in the statement because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But as you recall it was a luxurious car; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't an army car, and that's what it's about, right? It was just a normal car.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was a Volkswagen?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I've got to look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll look it up in a second. Do you recall this yellow rank? Can you describe it more vividly for us, please. Or the yellow insignia, actually, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right now. I have looked it up in a small book we had where the ranking of the Bosnian Serb army was in. So at that time I could see that it was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If -- if you had spent another five minutes, let's say, with this colonel, would you have been better able to describe him than you have today? For example, if you'd spent 10 minutes with him, do you think you'd be better able to describe him?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- it depends on the situation you meet people. I can describe you --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- you know, because this is an unpleasant situation, you're cross-examining me, and of course I know you, but I don't know the man who is sitting next to you. I can't describe him. So when it's -- it's in a stressful situation and you just have five minutes and there's a lot of going on at that time, I didn't write it down how -- how he looked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He was answering, I didn't want to cut him off.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you: This yellow emblem or insignia that you saw, did you see that on Colonel Beara on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I recall now, I saw something like that on his uniform, but I don't know whether it was the same symbol because it was a yellow symbol on the black uniform. I don't know whether it's correct, but you can -- you can of course look it up, whether there were soldiers wearing black uniforms with yellow insignias.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we will look it up. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd ask that the statement of the 24th of October, 1995, be placed on the ELMO and that the witness Lieutenant Colonel Egbers be given perhaps, if he wishes, the Dutch version of his statement, or the original version of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he should have the Dutch version available at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me put the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For whatever use he might need to make of it. And the English version is in e-court and should be already on the screen. It is. Yes. Which page do you want us to go to?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 6 again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think. But I'd like to offer the witness that he can look through the entire document for purposes of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I would like for him, while he's looking, to point out, if I may ask, where in fact in his statement in 1995 he states that Colonel Beara had a yellow insignia or emblem.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use the word "yellow." Do you want me to look for the word "yellow"?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What word did you use? Pink, red?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In his testimony a few minutes ago he did not use the word "yellow" in relation to Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then let me clarify that, Your Honour, and I apologise for that if I've misunderstood him. I wanted to know specifically from this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have every right to clarify it, but he never used the word "yellow" in relation --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just clarify, because I may have misunderstood him, Your Honour, not intentionally, believe me. And if I may just proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did Colonel Beara at any time have a yellow emblem or insignia on his uniform when you purportedly met him on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, but I've got to look it up what I've stated in 1995 -- in 1995 about this. But he was dressed in a uniform. That's what I can recall. Shall I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- one moment, because I think we need to be specific here. On page 79, line 24, your question, Mr. Ostojic, was the following: "This yellow insignia you were mentioning, did you see that on Colonel Beara on the 14th of July, 1995?" And his answer -- the witness's answer was: "I recall now I saw something like that on his uniform, but I don't know whether it was the same symbol, because it was a yellow symbol on the black uniform. And I don't know whether it's correct, but you can -- you can of course look it up, whether there were soldiers wearing black uniforms with yellow insignias." So that was his answer. So he never really agreed that -- that whatever he may have seen on Colonel Beara was a yellow insignia. But you can, of course, proceed with your line of questions on this matter to elicit further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think I have a question pending if I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Just direct our attention.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's page 7, and I describe there that on Friday, 14th of July, I made contact with Colonel Beara, and that's the -- that's the same military language that I've met him. I've spoken to him and he read the explanation. He -- where -- so he had -- he was a colonel for me. This man. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do see it, sir.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I could read it into the record, if the Court permits.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. I was reading it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll read it into the record so we have a clean transcript of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think it needs to be read, otherwise we'd have to have the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Great. "On Friday, 14th July 1995, I contacted Colonel Beara in the morning. I spoke to him. He read the statement and nothing was discussed. This man wore badges denoting he was a colonel. He wore camouflage uniform." There's obviously more which I'll get to in a minute. And if I can, with your permission, just stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to that specifically, that you have in front of you as well, and that I've read out you, you state that this man wore badges denoting he was a colonel. Can you describe the badges for us?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do that because we all had a UN book with the military ranking of the Bosnian Serb army in it, and it's -- it's a normal book and that's where the ranking is. I can't describe you the things he wore on his uniform, but I've looked it up and it was a colonel at that time. I don't have the book with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, do you have any independent recollection as to whether or not he had a yellow badge or a yellow insignia on his uniform; he, being Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he had a -- he wore the uniform of a colonel, and I don't know whether it was yellow, or pink as you call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I think that -- I apologise for the -- I think I was perhaps -- used the word "pink," and I think he's just responding to that and I apologise to the witness and to the Court for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, in any of your statements or testimonies did you ever testify that Colonel Beara had a yellow insignia or badge on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a black uniform - we discussed that - with a yellow insignia. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The black uniform with the yellow insignia was the other colonel; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was the other colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We don't know how tall he is, do you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
